title: chat edge gate and spark2 fallback

claims.text: chat.culture.dev sits behind a Cloudflare Worker that gates traffic at the edge, so anonymous traffic never reaches our machines and a real outage page shows when both sparks are down; when spark fails, signed-in people land on spark2 instead of a 500, after signing in again if needed

honesty_conditions.text: A simulated spark failure with Worker and spark2 in place returns the app, not a 500, to a signed-in test account

revisions.text: chat.culture.dev sits behind a Cloudflare Worker that accepts sign-in at the edge, so anonymous traffic never reaches our machines, and when spark fails signed-in people land on spark2 instead of a 500
revisions.reason: owner decided gate-only first: sign-in stays on the lens

claims.text: On 2026-11-03 signed-in users got 500s from LensConnectionLost for up to 41h after the Nov 2 00:44 reboot, while anonymous GET / still returned 200, and nothing alerted anyone

honesty_conditions.text: The dates and durations match the journal: first refusal Nov 2 00:44, restored Nov 3 17:58

claims.text: culture server start ignores a pidfile whose PID is not a culture process, so a reboot cannot wedge the IRCd; this ships before any failover work

honesty_conditions.text: With a pidfile pointing at another user's thread, culture server start succeeds; a test covers it

claims.text: The lens exposes a readiness check that fails when its IRCd is unreachable; failover and alerting key on it, not on / or /healthz

honesty_conditions.text: With the IRCd stopped the readiness check returns non-200, and with it running returns 200

claims.text: No per-request round-robin between instances: one person's session stays on one instance until that instance fails

honesty_conditions.text: Two requests from one session always reach the same instance while that instance is healthy

claims.text: Tunnel replicas are not the fallback mechanism: each host gets its own tunnel and the Worker chooses between them

honesty_conditions.text: spark and spark2 connect through different tunnel UUIDs

claims.text: A Worker on chat.culture.dev picks the origin, pins a session to it, fails over on origin failure, and serves a static outage page when both are down

honesty_conditions.text: Stopping both origins yields the static outage page, and the Worker stays within Free limits at current traffic

claims.text: Origin hostnames accept only the Worker's credential and the lens trusts a verifiable identity from it, so anonymous traffic never reaches our machines

honesty_conditions.text: A direct request to an origin hostname without the Worker's credential is refused before reaching the lens

claims.text: A single source of truth for sign-in, permissions and agent credentials must exist across both instances; separate guests.db files would sign people out on failover
On failover a person's nick changes from spark-<nick> to spark2-<nick> unless the design changes that
spark2 needs no guest sandbox or model path, because guest mode is off on standby; a second sbx would only be needed if guests are later served there

revisions.text: The failover site needs its own sbx IRCd and guest agents, and a model path that does not run through spark
revisions.reason: owner decided q3: approved users only on standby

claims.text: spark2 is provisioned with irc-lens config, cloudflared, its own secrets and a running IRCd, using the supported install verbs

honesty_conditions.text: culture console install and culture server install produce running units on spark2, reachable only through its tunnel

claims.text: This does not survive a home power or internet outage on the machines; only the Worker's static outage page does
Moved history is partial: a person failing over may see gaps because history is per-server and backfill replays only recent in-memory events
Owner decision 2026-11-03: warm standby on spark2 is enough; active-active sharing of live load is not wanted
Owner decision 2026-11-03: a person's nick may change from spark-<nick> to spark2-<nick> during failover
The service sends periodic pings to healthchecks.io using the grant secret CULTURE_HEALTHCHECK_URL, so an outage alerts even when our machines cannot send anything

honesty_conditions.text: Pings are sent only after a real IRCd readiness check passes, so a healthy landing page with a dead IRCd stops the pings
The check also alerts when the pinger's host is off, because silence alone turns it down

claims.text: The owner receives an hourly email while any health check is down, until it recovers

honesty_conditions.text: With the check down for over an hour, at least 2 reminder emails arrive at the owner's address

revisions.text: The owner receives an email every hour; exact trigger pending owner clarification

claims.text: After a reboot the standby rejoins the mesh without a person unlocking its keyring, because a locked keyring leaves spark2 with no link credentials

honesty_conditions.text: After a spark2 reboot with no human action, it links to at least one peer

claims.text: The owner as operator, and approved people who use chat.culture.dev as their mesh console

honesty_conditions.text: Every behaviour in this spec is observable by one of these two groups

claims.text: When spark fails, people reach spark2 after signing in again if needed, as spark2-<nick>; when both are down they see an outage page; the owner is told by email either way

honesty_conditions.text: Each clause is exercised in the failover drill: sign-in again, spark2 nick, outage page, email

claims.text: An IRCd outage behind a healthy landing page alerts the owner within 10 minutes, against about 41 hours unnoticed on 2026-11-03; a simulated spark failure serves signed-in people from spark2 within 5 minutes

honesty_conditions.text: Both timings are measured in a drill, not estimated

claims.text: Owner decision 2026-11-03: hourly email only while a check is down, using the healthchecks.io reminder setting; silence means healthy; no always-on status mail

Owner decision 2026-11-03: the Worker is gate-only first (routing, failover, outage page, keeping anonymous traffic off the origin); sign-in stays on the lens; identity in D1 is a later separate phase

spark2's standby lens holds a copy of accounts and permissions from spark's guests.db, one-way and refreshed on a schedule, because an empty store would refuse every approved person including the admin

honesty_conditions.text: After a copy, an approved person can sign in on spark2 and holds the same role and grants

claims.text: Owner decision 2026-11-03: /readyz covers the main IRC server only, so a guest sandbox failure never triggers failover for everyone; a separate sbx signal can come later

The health ping ships as part of the culture app: a CLI verb installs the timer on any host, reads the check URL from grant and the site address from the lens config, replacing the hand-written script and units on spark

honesty_conditions.text: On a host with only the culture install and the grant secret, the CLI verb alone produces a timer that pings healthchecks.io, reports /fail when /readyz fails, and spark runs on it with the hand-written files removed

claims.text: Browser POSTs work through the Worker: _origin_ok compares Origin to the request host, so a Worker fetching an origin hostname with a different Host gets every browser POST refused

honesty_conditions.text: A real browser signs in and sends a message through the Worker, on both origins

claims.text: Health pings check the primary's own local /readyz as well as the public one, so a failover can't hide that spark is down: after failover the public /readyz would answer 200 from spark2

honesty_conditions.text: With spark's IRCd stopped and traffic on spark2, the check goes down and hourly reminders arrive

claims.text: Failover trips only after several consecutive failed /readyz checks, and returning to spark is a deliberate step, so a routine restart can't bounce everyone onto a different nick

honesty_conditions.text: Restarting the console or IRCd during a deploy moves no one to spark2

claims.text: The Worker can be removed in one step: deleting its route restores direct access through the existing tunnel, and that path stays available until the Worker has proven itself

honesty_conditions.text: A rehearsed rollback restores signed-in service within 5 minutes

claims.text: The guests.db copy to spark2 stays private: it holds emails, password and token hashes, so it travels only over the tailnet or LAN, stays mode 0600 on spark2, and has the same retention as the original

honesty_conditions.text: After a copy, the file on spark2 is mode 0600 and no copy path crosses the public internet

claims.text: During failover people see rooms but no spark agents, media uploaded on spark is missing, and personal agent credentials issued for spark- nicks don't work; standby means keeping humans talking, not full service

Rate limits keep working through the Worker because same-zone subrequests keep the visitor's IP in CF-Connecting-IP, per Cloudflare docs; if the origin isn't same-zone they collapse to one IP and one visitor could lock out all sign-ins
Owner decision 2026-11-03: standby is approved users only, with no account changes and guest mode off. Guests get the outage message during a failover, and spark2 needs no guest sandbox or model path

open_vagueness.text: Whether Worker subrequests can reach tunnel hostnames behind an Access service token and hold SSE through the 10ms CPU limit; needs a spike
open_vagueness.resolution: Owner resolved 2026-11-03: the spike proved a Free-plan Worker can reach the tunnel through an Access service token and hold SSE for 5 minutes (scope s19). Route on chat.culture.dev, Access on the same hostname, second tunnel, failover and longer streams become plan acceptance tests.

open_vagueness.text: Whether remote-origin messages are written to the local history.db (agentirc), which decides how complete history looks after failover
Whether moving email and consent records to Cloudflare D1 requires a Terms/Privacy update (katvan legal pages not read)
Why spark has no established links to thor and orin after its restart (culture#510 suspected, unconfirmed)
Whether cf.resolveOverride keeps the Host header through the tunnel on this plan, or the lens must instead trust a configured public origin; needs a small POST spike before building

scope_entries.surface: spark journal + console log, 2026-11-03
scope_entries.finding: stale pidfile server-spark.pid held a PID reused as a thread of another user's process (xdg-document-portal); sbx and spark2 the same

scope_entries.surface: culture_core/cli/server.py:564 + pidfile.py:100
scope_entries.finding: _check_already_running calls is_process_alive only; kill(pid,0) PermissionError counts as alive; is_culture_process exists at pidfile.py:75 but is not called. No open issue for this; overview/renderer_web.py:139-154 can signal an unrelated PID

scope_entries.surface: irc-lens web/routes.py:1079-1088, session.py:429-446
scope_entries.finding: /healthz is a constant ok with no IRC check; connect() has one host, no retry; auto-reconnect is deliberately off, dead sessions return 503 on input

scope_entries.surface: irc-lens web/sessions.py:195-205, web/routes.py:746-756,975-980
scope_entries.finding: IRC sessions and SSE buses are in-memory per process, so a send on A never reaches a stream on B; affinity is assumed, unstated, and no stickiness code exists

scope_entries.surface: Cloudflare tunnel docs + tunnel API GET
scope_entries.finding: chat tunnel has one connector today; docs say replicas give no steering or stickiness and route to the closest one, and session affinity needs a separate tunnel per host

scope_entries.surface: culture.dev zone + account via CF API GET
scope_entries.finding: Free Website plan; Load Balancing API 403; existing Workers learn-api and lens-delivery-alert, 2 KV, 1 D1, no routes; docs: 10ms CPU, 100k req/day then error 1027, no wall-clock limit while client connected

scope_entries.surface: lens config auth.mode + web/auth.py:399
scope_entries.finding: auth.mode is cloudflare-access with app_signin enabled; no Worker-trust mode exists. Worker fetch through Access service token on a tunnel hostname is unverified and needs a spike

scope_entries.surface: irc-lens access_store.py:236-267, app_session.py:84-103,190-213, guest_store.py:60-101
scope_entries.finding: sessions, users, grants, agent_credentials, guests, consents all in one local rollback-journal SQLite file with a per-process read cache; unsafe over NFS; cookie is an opaque id so no key to share, but the row must exist

scope_entries.surface: agentirc client.py:469-476, irc-lens web/nickname.py:67-69, agent_nick.py, access_store.py:64-66
scope_entries.finding: NICK must start with the server name, hard-coded with no config switch; lens prefixes from server.name; grants key on email and survive, agent_credentials store the full prefixed nick and would not; no identity links spark-ori to spark2-ori

scope_entries.surface: docs/guest-sandbox.md:12-38 + ~/.culture/sandbox/*.yaml
scope_entries.finding: sbx is loopback, standalone, no-persist so a second copy is cheap but relocation of its agents is undocumented; both agents use gateway localhost:8001 on spark; models cortex-spark2 and worker-spark span both hosts

scope_entries.surface: spark2 over ssh; docs/durable-mesh.md:21-26, culture_core/cli/console.py:696
scope_entries.finding: spark2 has culture 14.11.1 (spark 14.13.0), grant, no cloudflared, no ~/.config/irc-lens; culture console install exists; server crash-looping on the stale pidfile

scope_entries.surface: ip route on spark and spark2
scope_entries.finding: both hosts use the same home router as default gateway, so they share a LAN and uplink; correction: an older note that spark2's gateway is spark is stale

scope_entries.surface: docs/reference/server/architecture.md:120,166,181-183, agentirc ircd.py:59, server_link.py:975-1008
scope_entries.finding: HistoryStore is local SQLite; event log is a 10000-entry in-memory deque; whether remote-origin messages land in local history.db is unknown

scope_entries.surface: grant on spark and spark2
scope_entries.finding: CULTURE_HEALTHCHECK_URL is set on spark (https, host hc-ping.com, value not printed); spark2's grant has no such secret, so a ping from spark2 needs it copied or a separate check URL

scope_entries.surface: culture-server-spark2 on spark2
scope_entries.finding: fixed 2026-11-03 16:18 UTC by moving the stale pidfile aside after confirming its PID was a thread of another user's process and 6667 was not listening; server now listens on spark2's tailnet address

scope_entries.surface: mesh links on spark, thor, orin, spark2
scope_entries.finding: 2026-11-03 18:2x: all peer ports reachable from spark, but no established server-to-server sockets on spark, thor or orin; spark logged Linking to thor/orin once with no follow-up, thor/orin logged nothing; spark2 login keyring Locked=true, logging No credential found for all peers. Cause on spark side unconfirmed; matches culture#510 no-retry shape

scope_entries.surface: spark restart 18:22 and agentirc ircd.py:521-532
scope_entries.finding: restart logged Linking to all three peers including spark2, yet zero peer sockets on spark, thor or orin and nothing in the thor/orin server logs; connect_to_peer spawns link.handle as a background task, so a failed handshake may be silent. Restart did not restore federation; cause unconfirmed

scope_entries.surface: irc-lens web/app_session.py:100-103, access_store.py:59-78
scope_entries.finding: with gate-only sign-in on the lens, spark2 opens its own guests.db; unknown session ids mean signed out and an empty users table means no approved people, so failover needs at least a copied store. This follows from the owner's gate-first decision and was not explicit in the options offered

scope_entries.surface: Worker spike, workers.dev to chat.culture.dev tunnel, 2026-11-03
scope_entries.finding: PASSED: a throwaway Worker reached the tunnel hostname with an Access service token (login 303 with session cookie) and held GET /events open as text/event-stream for the full 300s, 20 chunks, on the Free plan, with no CPU-limit error; Worker deleted afterwards. NOT tested: a Worker route on chat.culture.dev itself, Access in front of that same hostname, a second tunnel, failover between origins, or streams longer than 5 minutes

scope_entries.surface: spark ~/.culture/healthcheck-ping.sh and culture-healthcheck units
scope_entries.finding: the working ping is hand-installed on spark, hardcodes chat.culture.dev, and isn't in any repo; the owner decided it belongs in the app. culture_core/cli/console.py already has an install verb, so this is the likely home, to confirm while planning

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: irc-lens web/routes.py _origin_ok, web/csrf.py
scope_entries.finding: Origin must equal the request host. Cloudflare docs: changing the fetch URL hostname changes Host, while cf.resolveOverride keeps Host but needs both hosts in the zone. The spike only sent GETs, so this was untested and every send would have returned 403. Whether the tunnel ingress and resolveOverride combine on this plan is unknown

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / observability lens: ~/.culture/healthcheck-ping.sh
scope_entries.finding: the ping script probes the public URL only. It is correct today, but once the Worker fails over, a dead spark IRCd with a live spark host would keep reporting healthy, which silently defeats the owner's hourly email during standby

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / failure-mode lens: this session's deploy
scope_entries.finding: restarting the IRCd and console took seconds, and the spec states no threshold or failback rule, so a plain deploy could trigger failover and change everyone's nick

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / reversibility lens: spec c8 and tunnel config
scope_entries.finding: c8 locks origins to the Worker's credential, but nothing states how to undo it. Worker bugs, Free-plan error 1027 or an expired service token would be a full outage with no way around

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: irc-lens guest_store.py, access_store.py
scope_entries.finding: the store holds consents, password hashes, token hashes and audit rows, and c25 says only that it is copied

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / overlooked-actors lens: systemd units on spark, web/store.py, access_store.py:64-66
scope_entries.finding: all 4 mesh agents and the media directory live only on spark, and agent_credentials store the full prefixed nick. Cross-server rooms also need #519 fixed, since mesh links are down today

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: irc-lens web/entry.py:291,426
scope_entries.finding: client_ip reads only CF-Connecting-IP and drives sign-in, guest and deletion limits. The documented same-zone behaviour is untested here, as the spike ran from workers.dev

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / adjacent-systems lens: spark2 gateway
scope_entries.finding: spark2 has nothing on port 8001, and both sandbox agents use gateway localhost:8001, confirming c11: guests on spark2 have no model path until that's built

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / operations lens: Worker quota
scope_entries.finding: clean for now: the console logged 71 requests in 24h against 100k per day. Residual: each request counts, and Worker service token expiry needs an owner

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / security lens: cookies and Turnstile
scope_entries.finding: clean: cookies are Secure and host-only and passed through in the spike. Turnstile wasn't exercised, and its behaviour through a Worker is unexamined

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / migration lens: guests.db schema
scope_entries.finding: tables use additive CREATE IF NOT EXISTS migrations, so a copy from a newer spark to an older spark2 lens is unexamined: both hosts need matching versions, to be a plan risk

scope_entries.surface: t2 POST spike, same-zone Worker route, 2026-11-04
scope_entries.finding: MEASURED: browser-style POST through a same-zone Worker returned 204 with the public Origin and 403 with a foreign one, on Host chat. The lens recorded a Cloudflare Worker IPv6 address as the client, not the visitor's IP, so c34's same-zone assumption is false here and all visitors would share one rate-limit bucket. resolveOverride was only tried against the same host, so reaching a second tunnel is still untested

lapses.what: The Worker spike sent only GETs, so it didn't cover the POST path, yet I reported it as proving the riskiest assumption; the Origin check shows POSTs could fail
